title: Key invariant: the guided well-ordered subsets form a chain (Zermelo's well-ordering theorem)
intent: Prove Zermelo's well-ordering theorem (from the axiom of choice every hSet carries a well-ordering) by carrying the whole argument on one auxiliary notion, the 'guided' well-ordered subsets — those whose elements are the choice function's picks — and on their invariant, that these guided subsets form a chain under inclusion; the main theorem then becomes a skeleton that applies this invariant and a small set of surrounding lemmas.

parent.name: ZermeloWellOrdering
parent.statement: Theorem ZermeloWellOrdering {X:hSet} : AxiomOfChoice ⇒ ∃ R : hrel X, isWellOrder R.

children.name: guided_WOSubset_total
children.statement:
Lemma guided_WOSubset_total {X:hSet} (g : choice_fun X) :
  LEM -> is_wosubset_chain (guidedFamily g).
children.closed_by: proof_by_contradiction on W ≡ C ∨ W ≡ D (via isInterval, which gives the two guided points c, d whose guided-ness equations gC c and gD d contradict), then each disjunct assembles C ≼ D or D ≼ C from the common-initial data WCD, WCi, WDi
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: Assuming LEM, the guided well-ordered subsets of X form a chain.

children.name: chain_union_le
children.statement:
Lemma chain_union_le {X:hSet} {I:UU} (S : I -> WOSubset X) (Schain : is_wosubset_chain S) :
  ∀ i, S i ≼ ⋃ Schain.
children.closed_by: exists (subtype_union_containedIn S i); split; the order-compatibility is pr2 (chain_union_tosub_le _ i), the initial-segment part is chain_union_rel_initial
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: Every member of a chain of well-ordered subsets sits below the union.

children.name: upto'_eqn
children.statement:
Lemma upto'_eqn {X:hSet} (g : choice_fun X) (C D : WOSubset X) (j : C ≼ D)
      (c : C) (d : D) :
  pr1 (subtype_inc (pr1 j) c) = pr1 d ->
  pr1 (g (upto' c)) = pr1 (g (upto' d)).
children.closed_by: assert e' : upto' c = upto' d by subtypePath_prop, reducing to upto c = upto d, then upto_eqn under induction e'
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: If subtype_inc j c = d then the guided choices of upto' c and upto' d agree.

children.name: WOSubset_plus_point
children.statement:
Definition WOSubset_plus_point {X:hSet}
           (S:WOSubset X) (z:X) (nSz : ¬ S z) : LEM -> WOSubset X
  := λ lem, subtype_plus S z,,
            TOSrel (TOSubset_plus_point S z nSz),,
            TOtotal (TOSubset_plus_point S z nSz),,
            hasSmallest_WOSubset_plus_point S z nSz lem.
children.closed_by: a definitional assembly: subtype_plus S z paired with the order of TOSubset_plus_point (TOSrel, TOtotal) and the smallest-element proof hasSmallest_WOSubset_plus_point S z nSz lem
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: Appending a point z to a well-ordered subset, assuming LEM, gives a well-ordered subset.

children.name: TOSubset_plus_point_incl
children.statement:
Lemma TOSubset_plus_point_incl {X:hSet} (S:TOSubset X) (z:X) (nSz : ¬ S z) :
  S ⊆ TOSubset_plus_point S z nSz.
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: A totally ordered subset is included in the subset with one point added.

children.name: TOSubset_plus_point_le
children.statement:
Lemma TOSubset_plus_point_le {X:hSet} (S:TOSubset X) (z:X) (nSz : ¬ S z) :
  S ≼ TOSubset_plus_point S z nSz.
children.closed_by: use tpair; [apply TOSubset_plus_point_incl | intros s t le; exact le]
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: Adding a point preserves the order-inclusion relation.

children.name: TOSubset_plus_point_initial
children.statement:
Lemma TOSubset_plus_point_initial {X:hSet} (S:TOSubset X) (z:X) (nSz : ¬ S z) :
  sub_initial (TOSubset_plus_point_incl S z nSz).
children.closed_by: intros s t Ss Tt le; squash Tt to St or ezt; [exact St | fromempty le]
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: The old subset is an initial segment of the subset with one point added.

applicability.goal_shape: An existence theorem of the shape AxiomOfChoice ⇒ ∃ R : hrel X, isWellOrder R (more generally, build a maximal or universal object by a Zorn-style maximality argument) where the object cannot be built all at once but its totality follows from maximality.
applicability.use_when: There is a notion of 'good' or 'guided' approximation that is closed under unions of chains, and every non-universal approximation extends by one element. State the invariant (the approximations form a chain) as its own lemma, and let the main proof be a skeleton over it plus the extension lemmas.
applicability.avoid_when: The approximations do not form a chain, or the invariant lemma itself is the hard part and does not decompose further (here guided_WOSubset_total is 190 lines — the move concentrates, not removes, the difficulty); or a direct transfinite recursion is more natural than a maximality argument.

claims.claim: The authors name the auxiliary notion that carries the argument: "Given a choice function g, we single out well ordered subsets C of X that follow the choice functions advice when constructed by adding one element at a time to the top. We may say that C is 'guided' by g."

consequences: The move concentrates the difficulty into the invariant lemma guided_WOSubset_total (190 lines) and reduces the main theorem to a 95-line skeleton that applies it. It creates the obligation to show the union of a chain of guided subsets is itself guided (and well ordered via chain_union_WOSubset), and to transport the induced well-ordering from the maximal guided subset W back to the whole set X through an hSet univalence equivalence. Failure mode: if the invariant is left as a single opaque block, the decomposition buys nothing — the children (upto'_eqn, the TOSubset_plus_point lemmas, chain_union_le) must be standalone lemmas for the invariant to be re-assembled and re-used.
